answers.q1: pnpm (pinned by packageManager pnpm@12.9.1; the preinstall script enforces it with only-allow pnpm; Node ^20.19.0 || >=22.12.0). Install with: pnpm install (CONTRIBUTING.md uses `pnpm i`). CI then runs `pnpm run build` before testing.
answers.q2: pnpm run test. This runs `pnpm test-unit && pnpm test-serve && pnpm test-build`. The e2e parts need Playwright Chromium, so run `pnpm playwright install chromium` and `pnpm run build` first. CI also runs `pnpm run test-serve-bundled`, which `pnpm run test` doesn't include. If you only want the unit suite, use `pnpm run test-unit`.
answers.q3: pnpm exec vitest run packages/vite/src/node/__tests__/config.spec.ts (equivalent: pnpm run test-unit packages/vite/src/node/__tests__/config.spec.ts). Either way this uses the root vitest.config.ts.
answers.q4: Run these in order, as the CI lint job does: pnpm run build && pnpm run lint && pnpm format && git diff --exit-code && pnpm run typecheck && pnpm run test-docs. `pnpm run lint` is eslint, `pnpm format` is oxfmt, and the `git diff --exit-code` after it fails if formatting changed anything. In this checkout `git diff` won't work because it is not a git repository. Use `pnpm exec oxfmt --check` instead for the formatting check.
answers.q5: I found no committed generated or vendored directory that I could confirm. These are the nearest things I found. Build output is git-ignored and must not be edited: dist/ and dist-ssr/ (including packages/*/dist), plus playground-temp/, temp/, .eslintcache and packages/vite/LICENSE (git-ignored, created at build time). pnpm-lock.yaml is generated by pnpm and the formatter ignores it. packages/*/CHANGELOG.md files are produced by the release tooling. Test fixtures (**/fixtures/**, **/*.snap) and the minified or third-party files under playground/ (for example slash@3.0.0.js) are deliberate test inputs, so leave them unchanged. packages/create-vite/template-* is excluded from lint, but it holds the real template source, so those files are hand-edited. I did not look for vendored code under packages/vite/src, so I can't rule it out.
